Condo Board President here, uncompensated. I'm also the self-appointed litter-picker-upper, because litter is my pet peeve. Fortunately, we only have about 6 1/2 acres.

A condominium is a corporation where the owners each own their apartments, or "individual elements", and share ownership of the grounds, amenities, and other property, called "common elements". The corporation has a Board of Directors, similar to most corporations. It is made up of owners, and elected by the owners. 3-7 members is typical; ours has 5.

In theory, the Board sets policy, and a management company implements policy. This is similar to a legislature and bureaucracy in multiparty government, or the party and the state in one-party government. In practice, the Board typically winds up with much more responsibility than just decision-making, because lots of things fall between the cracks, or cannot be fit into the budget. Consequently, board members and helpful volunteers pick up litter, watch for criminal behavior, assist elderly and disabled residents, etc.
